summary: James Darmesteter worked in Iranian and Central Asian studies, Indology, and linguistics. Educated at Lycée Condorcet and École Pratique des Hautes Études under Bergaigne, Bréal, and Hauvette-Besnault, he taught at EPHE (director in 1892) and Collège de France (1885–1894).

James Drummond Anderson worked in Indology and linguistics. He studied at Cheltenham College, Rugby School, and the University of Cambridge (M.A. c. 1907–1909), served in the Indian Civil Service (1875–1900), and lectured in Bengali at Cambridge from 1907.

James Duerlinger is a scholar of philosophy, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He studied at the University of Wisconsin–Madison (c. 1964–1968) and under Sheldon Pollock, later becoming Professor Emeritus at the University of Iowa, where he joined in 1971.
James Dwight Dana studied at Yale College from c. 1830 to 1833. He later held a post at Yale University from c. 1850 to 1892.

James Fairbrother Edwards worked in religious studies and Indology. He studied at Handsworth Theological College from c. 1905 to 1908 and served as Principal of the United Theological College in Pune starting in 1930.

James Fergusson worked in history, archaeology, and Indology. Educated at the Royal High School, he became a member of the Royal Asiatic Society in 1840 and served as secretary to A. H. Layard at the Office of Works in 1868.

James Fieser works in philosophy and religious studies. He studied at Berea College (c. 1976–1980) and Purdue University (c. 1983–1988), and has held posts at the University of Tennessee at Martin and the University of Tennessee, Knoxville.

James Fuller Blumhardt worked in Indology and linguistics. He served as Lecturer in Bengali at the University of Cambridge (1883–1888) and University College London (c. 1896–1922), and worked at the British Museum from c. 1894 to 1921.

James G. Mullens works in Buddhist and religious studies. He studied at Simon Fraser, Victoria, and McMaster universities under Graeme MacQueen, Yün-hua Jan, and John G. Arapura, and held a post at the University of Saskatchewan in 1989.

James Grant Liston Garthwaite worked in linguistics and Indology. After earning a B.A. at Westminster College, London, he served as a missionary and teacher with the Basel Mission (c. 1857–1860) and became a Fellow of the University of Madras in 1884.
James Grant Stephen worked in linguistics and Indology. He earned a B.A. from the University of Cambridge (c. 1857–1861), where he also served as Lecturer in Hindustani from 1860 to 1863.

James Gray worked in Indology and Buddhist studies. He taught at Akyab Government High School (1872), was Professor of Pāli at Basic Education High School No. 1 Dagon (c. 1876), and served as Professor of Pali at Rangoon University (c. 1884–1905).

James H. Austin is a specialist in Buddhist studies and medicine. He trained with Nanrei Sohaku Kobori and Katsujo Terayama, and held positions at the University of Oregon, University of Colorado, University of Idaho, and University of Florida.

James Hadley worked in linguistics and Indology. He studied at Fairfield Academy and Yale (under Edward Elbridge Salisbury), later serving as tutor at Middlebury College (1845) and Assistant Professor at Yale University from 1845 to 1872.

James Hair Maclean worked in religious studies and Indology. He studied at the universities of Glasgow, Oxford, and Jena, and served as a missionary for the United Free Church of Scotland beginning in 1895.

James Hartzell worked in Indology, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology. He held posts at Columbia University (c. 2001–2007), the University of Manitoba (c. 2008–2009), the University of Trento (c. 2010), and the Basque Center on Cognition, Brain and Language.

James Haughton Woods worked in Indology and philosophy. He studied at Harvard, Episcopal Divinity School, Berlin, Oxford, and Strasbourg, also training under Deussen, Venis, Adkar, and Lanman. He served at Harvard as Assistant in History (1891) and Professor (1913–1934).

James Heitzman was a historian and Indologist who studied at the University of Pennsylvania and Drexel University. He held posts at the Library of Congress, Cazenovia College, Georgia State University, and the University of California, Davis.
James Henry Nelson was an Indologist. He earned an M.A. from the University of Cambridge in 1856 and held a post as Fellow at King's College London.

James Hope Moulton worked in Iranian and Central Asian studies, linguistics, and religious studies. Educated at London, Edinburgh, and Cambridge (under Edward Byles Cowell), he held posts at Didsbury College (1902) and the University of Manchester (1908).
